name: Leigh Syndrome with Nephrotic Syndrome
aliases: Subacute Necrotizing Encephalomyelopathy with Nephrotic Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Modified Rahman Criteria for Leigh Syndrome

criteria.description: Progressive neurological symptoms including psychomotor regression and hypotonia
Bilateral symmetric lesions in basal ganglia and/or brainstem on MRI
Elevated lactate levels in blood and/or cerebrospinal fluid
Clinical and laboratory evidence of nephrotic syndrome including proteinuria and hypoalbuminemia
Identification of pathogenic variants in mitochondrial or nuclear genes associated with Leigh syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive neurological symptoms with characteristic neuroimaging findings and biochemical evidence of mitochondrial dysfunction plus clinical evidence of nephrotic syndrome
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic confirmation supports diagnosis but is not mandatory if clinical and imaging criteria are met.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Bilateral symmetric necrotic lesions in basal ganglia
searchTerms: dead tissue spots in brain movement centers
basal ganglia brain lesions on both sides
high protein levels in urine indicating kidney damage
high lactate in blood or spinal fluid
high blood pressure from kidney disease
renal involvement leading to high blood pressure
protein in urine without full kidney disease

laboratory: Elevated lactate in blood and cerebrospinal fluid
Elevated serum creatinine in advanced renal involvement
imaging: Bilateral symmetric hyperintense lesions in basal ganglia and brainstem on T2-weighted MRI
genetic: Pathogenic variants in mitochondrial DNA genes (e.g., MT-ATP6)
Nuclear gene mutations affecting mitochondrial function (e.g., SURF1, NDUFS4)
other: Renal biopsy demonstrating focal segmental glomerulosclerosis or minimal change disease

distinguishingFeatures: No characteristic basal ganglia lesions on MRI
Primary renal pathology without mitochondrial dysfunction

redFlags: Rapidly progressive neurological deterioration in infancy
Onset of nephrotic syndrome concurrent with neurological decline
Elevated lactate levels indicating mitochondrial dysfunction
references: Rahman S, et al. Leigh syndrome: clinical features and biochemical and DNA abnormalities. Ann Neurol. 1996.
Finsterer J. Leigh and Leigh-like syndrome in children and adults. Pediatr Neurol. 2008.
Orphanet Report on Leigh syndrome with nephrotic syndrome, ORPHA:255249.
